setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter named on the call. The only pre-call artefact referenced is a written application: 'I saw that you already wrote a few things down, but I would like to hear just everything from you.'

prospect.name: Alexandre Lesbats
prospect.occupation: Fifteen years in the spirits industry; travels internationally every three to four weeks including to Asia, entertains clients over dinner, presents to audiences regularly
prospect.family_status: Married; two daughters aged seven and six. Wife recently changed to a lower-paying job she is passionate about; a car purchase of around 20k is pending.
prospect.training_background: Started at 83 kg in 2019-20 and dropped to 63-64 kg largely through basement kettlebell work and a keto-style diet; now 68-69 kg with more muscle. Trains four to six days a week — calisthenics (weighted pull-ups with a 13 kg vest, dips), running (10K in about 40-43 minutes, half marathon booked for November), and kettlebells (60 kg farmer carry, 20 kg Turkish get-up). Did Olympic weightlifting at around 16. Currently following a self-built programme generated with ChatGPT and fed with Whoop data. Owns 12, two 16s and a 20 kg kettlebells plus a pull-up and dip bar. Has never worked with a coach or trainer.
prospect.medical: No injuries and never majorly injured — 'I have never been majorly injured, never broke a bone'. Minor niggles only: pain under the foot when running beyond about 35 km a week, one shoulder less mobile than the other, and self-described weak wrists that limit heavy Turkish get-ups. Poor hip mobility and cannot touch the floor with straight legs.

signals: Already fit and highly disciplined — six years without missing a training week, including while travelling: 'I still never done a week without training'
Explicitly chasing the last increment rather than a rescue: 'I never had, like, the body I wanted to have... never saw my abs in my entire life'
Achievement-driven identity across domains: 'I always want to achieve more... whether it's for work or being better at something'
Optimises health as a hobby — creatine, magnesium, eight hours of sleep, blue-light blockers, a Whoop
Counter-signal to a pure optimizer read: price was a genuine barrier here, not a quality signal — he had 1.5k in mind against a 5.2k euro ask and a competing 20k car purchase

goals.text: See his abs for the first time in his life and lose the fat around his hips
Add size to arms and upper body — 'being a more muscular, I think I would like to as well'
Fix poor hip and shoulder mobility and general stiffness — cannot touch the floor with straight legs
Be a hybrid athlete able to do everything — run, swim, lift
Stop having to think about programming — 'I just don't want to think about my training... a kind of system that's easy to use'
Own a system he can run indefinitely without a coach — 'a kind of a system that I can kind of use after, like indefinitely'
Be proud of himself and be a model his daughters are proud of — 'I want to also share that with my kids'
Do Hyrox with his daughter at 50 and stay healthy as long as possible

pains.text: Six years of consistent training and he has still never achieved the body he wants — 'sometimes it's frustrating, never manage to be as fit as I want it to be'

Has hit the ceiling of his own knowledge and has nobody to correct him — 'maybe there's something I'm doing wrong, maybe I'm overtraining, but as long as not somebody will tell that to me, I may feel I'm right doing so'
His AI-generated programme agrees with him rather than challenging him — 'it tells you what you want to hear... never keep his position'
Evening hunger crash leading to overeating bread and butter before dinner — 'sometimes the mind is too strong for that, or too weak'
Wife's snacking habits pull him off his own nutrition — 'sometimes I could fall for an ice cream with her'
Poor mobility and stiffness in hips and shoulders, plus weak wrists limiting heavy kettlebell work
Heavy travel schedule and a 5.45am training window before children and work
Mental load of deciding what to train each morning — 'sometimes in the morning I say, damn, what should I do?'
Competing capital demands: a 20k car purchase and a wife who has just moved to a lower-paying job

objections.raw_quote: To be honest, in all honesty, I thought it was, I didn't have that price point in mind... I have never done training. So that's quite some money.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it ('do you feel like, out of the investment being on the bigger side, it is something I see myself doing?'), justified the premium via Trevor's standing, tested worth ('is that worth the 5.2k for you?' — yes), asked what he had set aside (1.5k), used the airplane oxygen-mask frame on investing in himself, then dropped to a $1,000 community tier.

objections.raw_quote: That's something I will also, as we share everything with my wife, need to discuss also with my wife, but yeah, that was not what I had in mind
objections.rep_response: Ran part of the play — asked what her thoughts would be and what she would find nice about it, surfaced that he is the money manager of the household, then used the oxygen-mask analogy about putting himself first. Never asked whether she would object to him being stronger, and never asked whether this was genuinely her decision or permission-seeking.

objections.raw_quote: family, and a new car that needs to be purchased, and those kind of things that are at the moment, because my wife just changed job... we need to purchase a new car as well, that's already a 20k investment, so on top of that, I'm fully transparent, that's quite a big investment to add on that at the moment
objections.rep_response: Asked what he had set aside, got 1.5k, then offered the $1,000 tier as a fit for that budget rather than working the financial picture further.

objections.raw_quote: because I place on, you know, I do kind of investments and stuff and so I don't have all the money available right now except for, how to say, you know, safety and stuff like that. And as we are already half of the month, I'm waiting for that for the next paycheck.
objections.rep_response: Pointed out he was throwing away half a month, then asked 'what do you have available so you can get started and we just split it up?' The prospect declined and held to the end of the month.

objections.raw_quote: That's the reason why it's really simple. I never say yes on the call, whether it's on the phone, whether it's on video. I used to work in sales as well. And I never say yes on the call.
objections.rep_response: Asked what was stopping him from starting and calling his wife afterwards, then accepted the principle without challenging it — 'I'm not going to force you to do anything. It sounds like you're serious. It's not like it's a getaway card' — and asked when he expected to pay.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No plan was structured. After the prospect said he would wait for his paycheck, the rep offered to split the already-reduced $1,000: 'What do you have available so you can get started and we just split it up? What would be a possible amount for you?' The prospect declined.

evidence: Verbally agreed to the $1,000 tier — 'So do you feel like, yeah, that is something I see myself doing? — Yeah, definitely, yeah.' and later 'I'm really serious about going with the program'

But no payment link was sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply. The rep explicitly deferred it: 'by the end of the month, come back... I can send you the payment link, and we can get you started at that point.'
He refused to transact on the call as a matter of policy: 'I never say yes on the call... I'm quite methodical in everything'
He also has to speak to his wife first: 'I share everything with my wife, so call my wife, say that I found the program'
Cash timing is a real constraint — he is waiting for a paycheck around the 27th-28th and declined an offer to split the payment to start sooner
Counter-evidence on intent is strong: he asked detailed scope questions about what is included, confirmed he already has a Skool account, and asked about ongoing programme progression
outcome.next_step: Prospect to discuss with his wife and pay for the $1,000 six-month community tier at the end of the month after his paycheck lands around the 27th-28th; rep to send the payment link then and grant Skool access. A personal check-in call in a month or two was also floated.

notable.note: The clearest example in this batch of the downsell pattern: $6,000 was quoted at 00:50:10, the prospect named a $1,500 ceiling at 00:56:46, and by 00:59:00 the price was $1,000 — an 83% reduction inside ten minutes, driven purely by the prospect's stated budget. The rep also actively dismantled his own consequence frame at 00:56:20, telling the prospect that if he had still been 83 kg he would have needed this, but 'that's not the case at the moment'. The discovery, goals work and commitment check on this call were genuinely strong; the money phase gave the whole value back.

quality.notes: Extensive inversion. The rep's own opening question appears under the prospect's label at 00:00:54 and 00:01:10, the prospect's answers appear under the rep at 00:05:06, 00:09:06, 00:11:31 and 00:30:00, and the crucial exchange at 01:04:43-01:04:55 has the rep's question and the prospect's answer swapped. Roles resolved from content throughout. Transcription also garbles terms ('apps' for 'abs', 'school' for Skool, 'caliber'/'kinesthetics' for calisthenics).
